q: Where should the cannula go for breast surgery?
why: Keep the operative side free for the surgeon and avoid lymphatic damage.

q: Which block suits breast surgery with axillary involvement?
why: PECS II covers the pectoral nerves and the axilla; a paravertebral is an alternative.

q: Why give antiemetics early for breast surgery?
o: Young women having breast surgery are at high PONV risk
why: Female sex and opioid use put many of these patients at high Apfel risk.

q: What provides most of the analgesia for a simple wide local excision?
why: Superficial surgery is well covered by infiltration plus simple analgesia.

q: How can intraoperative fentanyl be titrated under spontaneous ventilation?
why: A rising respiratory rate under spontaneous ventilation suggests more analgesia is needed.
